listening.script: Welcome to the city highlights tour. Before we begin our journey today, I would like to share a few important details about our schedule. First, our main bus will leave the station at nine fifteen sharp, instead of the original time of nine o'clock, due to brief road maintenance. Our first stop will be the historic castle built in the fourteenth century, where we will spend about one hour exploring the outer gardens. After that, we will head down to the old harbour for a fresh seafood lunch. Please note that lunch is included in your tour ticket, but drinks must be purchased separately at the restaurant. In the afternoon, you will have two hours of free time to shop in the local craft market. If anyone gets separated from the group, our final meeting point will be outside the central clock tower at four thirty in the afternoon. Have a wonderful trip!

listening.script: Welcome everyone to today’s briefing regarding our revised remote work policy starting next quarter. Following extensive feedback, the executive board has decided to transition from a full work-from-home setup to a hybrid model. Employees will now be required to spend three mandatory days in the office, specifically Tuesdays, Wednesdays, and Thursdays, while Mondays and Fridays remain flexible. To accommodate this shift, we are reallocating our annual transportation budget to provide monthly commuting stipends rather than reimbursing individual parking receipts. Furthermore, productivity will no longer be measured strictly by logged hours. Instead, quarterly performance reviews will focus entirely on project deliverables and key result areas. We believe this outcome-oriented framework fosters greater accountability and autonomy. Please note that all desk booking requests for team collaboration spaces must be submitted via the internal portal at least forty-eight hours in advance to avoid scheduling conflicts.

reading.title: Uyqu nima uchun muhim
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol
reading.text: Scientists have long known that sleep is essential, but recent studies show how deeply it affects daily life. Adults who sleep fewer than six hours a night are more likely to feel stressed and to make mistakes at work. A survey of 2,000 office workers found that those who slept seven to eight hours were twice as productive as colleagues who slept less. Some people believe that sleeping late at weekends can repair the damage of a short week, but researchers say this only helps partially. Experts recommend keeping regular bedtimes and avoiding screens for an hour before sleep.

items.exp: Matn: more likely to feel stressed. True.

items.q: The survey included 2,000 office workers.
items.exp: Matn: A survey of 2,000 office workers. True.

items.q: Sleeping late at weekends fully repairs a short week.
items.exp: Matn: this only helps partially. False.

items.exp: Sut haqida matnda gap yo'q. Not Given.

reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: Local business owners experienced a permanent decrease in total revenue after vehicle restrictions were introduced.
items.exp: Noto'g'ri. Matnda 'While some business owners initially feared a drop in income, overall revenue has actually risen by fifteen percent' deb ko'rsatilgan, ya'ni daromad kamaymagan, aksincha 15 foizga oshgan.

items.q: Money collected from vehicle parking fees is used to maintain local trails and historic buildings.
items.exp: To'g'ri. Matndagi 'The revenue generated from municipal parking fees is reinvested directly into maintaining local hiking trails and preserving traditional timber architecture' jumlasiga ko'ra, to'xtash joyi tushumlari so'qmoqlar va me'morchilikni saqlashga sarflanadi.

items.exp: Berilmagan. Matnda qo'shni qishloqlar raqamli tizim xarajatlarini tanqid qilgani ('neighboring villages have criticized the high operational costs') aytilgan, ammo ularning kelasi yili shunday tizim joriy etish rejalari haqida ma'lumot yo'q.

items.q: What was the primary reason local authorities introduced new vehicle regulations in 2021?
opts: To force visitors to buy digital loyalty passes
To reduce the negative environmental impact of tourist traffic
To fund the construction of modern cable cars
To generate extra income for local business owners
items.exp: To'g'ri javob B. Matnda ta'kidlanishicha: 'Local authorities implemented strict vehicle regulations in 2021 to combat the environmental impact of increased tourist traffic'.

reading.text:
Over the past decade, eco-tourism has transformed the small alpine village of Lauterbrunnen from a quiet seasonal destination into a year-round travel hotspot. Located in a steep Swiss valley known for its 72 waterfalls, the village traditionally relied on summer hiking and winter skiing. However, recent local initiatives have encouraged tourists to engage in sustainable activities, such as guided electric-bike tours and farm-to-table dining experiences.

Local authorities implemented strict vehicle regulations in 2021 to combat the environmental impact of increased tourist traffic. Visitors are now required to park their cars outside the main village area and rely on public electric buses or walking. While some business owners initially feared a drop in income, overall revenue has actually risen by fifteen percent. The revenue generated from municipal parking fees is reinvested directly into maintaining local hiking trails and preserving traditional timber architecture.

Furthermore, the local tourism board introduced a digital loyalty pass for visitors staying longer than three nights. This pass grants free access to municipal museums and discounts on regional cable cars. Although the initiative has successfully increased the average length of stay, neighboring villages have criticized the high operational costs of maintaining such digital programs. Nevertheless, Lauterbrunnen remains a pioneering model for sustainable tourism in mountainous regions.
reading.en: Sustainable Tourism in an Alpine Village

reading.title: Zamonaviy mehnatda asinxron muloqot modeli
reading.meta: True / False / Not Given · 4 ta savol

items.q: Constant synchronous interaction has been found to disrupt focused, uninterrupted work.
items.exp: Matnda "constant connectivity often induces cognitive fatigue and fragments deep work" deb ta'kidlangan, ya'ni doimiy aloqa diqqatni jamlab ishlash jarayonini buzadi.

items.q: Managers in asynchronous workplaces are encouraged to monitor active working hours more closely.
items.exp: Matnga ko'ra, rahbarlar faol soatlarni kuzatish kabi nazorat usullaridan voz kechishlari kerak ("Leaders must relinquish traditional modes of surveillance, such as tracking active hours").

items.q: Asynchronous workflows significantly reduce overall operational financial expenses for most companies.
items.exp: Matnda asinxron ish shaklining moslashuvchanlikka ta'siri haqida so'z yuritilgan bo'lsa-da, kompaniyaning moliyaviy xarajatlarini kamaytirishi haqida ma'lumot berilmagan.

items.q: According to the passage, how can information asymmetry be prevented in geographically dispersed teams?
opts: By meticulously documenting and archiving all operational protocols
By relying strictly on output-based financial incentives
By tracking employees' active working hours continuously
By holding more frequent synchronous virtual meetings
items.exp: Matndagi "every operational protocol must be meticulously archived to prevent information asymmetry" jumlasiga ko'ra, axborot tengsizligining oldini olish uchun barcha ish tartiblari batafsil hujjatlashtirilishi shart.

reading.text:
The contemporary corporate paradigm is undergoing a profound metamorphism, driven largely by the proliferation of asynchronous communication models. Historically, organizational efficacy relied heavily on synchronous interaction—real-time meetings, immediate messaging, and co-located collaboration. However, recent empirical research indicates that such constant connectivity often induces cognitive fatigue and fragments deep work. Asynchronous workflows, by contrast, empower employees to structure their tasks around personal peak productivity hours, fundamentally decoupling time spent from output generated.

Despite these theoretical advantages, transitioning to an asynchronous framework presents distinct managerial challenges. Leaders must relinquish traditional modes of surveillance, such as tracking active hours, and instead adopt output-based evaluation metrics. Furthermore, documentation becomes paramount; every operational protocol must be meticulously archived to prevent information asymmetry among geographically dispersed teams. While critics argue that asynchronous environments may inadvertently erode interpersonal camaraderie and organizational culture, proponents maintain that deliberate, scheduled social touchpoints can mitigate isolation without compromising individual autonomy. Ultimately, organizations that master this delicate equilibrium stand to gain unprecedented levels of workforce agility and talent retention, redefining the parameters of modern employment in an increasingly digitized global economy.
reading.en: Asynchronous Communication Models in Modern Employment

speaking:
